name: Origin Compliance Letter & Document Templates
note: Placeholders use {{DOUBLE_BRACES}}. Letter/cert templates (01-06) plus one fillable written-program template per KB standard (program-*). Each program-* template's section headings, training and recordkeeping lines are verbatim from its KB entry; fill the [[...]] prompts with company-specific procedure. Follow each grounding_rule.

templates.purpose: Cover letter transmitting a contractor's safety program package to a prequalification reviewer (ISN RAVS, Avetta, Veriforce, PEC) or a hiring client.
templates.grounding_rule: Every program in PROGRAM_LIST must exist as a KB entry and be cited by its exact citation. Never state an agency 'approved' a template; state the program 'meets the requirements of [citation].'

templates.purpose: Signed management certification page attached to the front of any written safety program, affirming it is implemented and reviewed. Reviewers look for an accountable signature and a review date.
templates.grounding_rule: CITATION must be the exact citation of the matching KB entry. The certification must name a real accountable person and a review cadence; do not leave the responsible-person field generic.

templates.purpose: Letter explaining an elevated Experience Modification Rate to a hiring client and documenting the corrective actions in progress. Used when EMR exceeds the client's threshold (often 1.00).
templates.grounding_rule: Describe EMR mechanics exactly as in the EMR KB entry (primary/excess, 3-year lagged period, frequency drives primary losses). Do not fabricate a projected EMR figure; use the value the user supplies or a stated range.

templates.purpose: Letter from the contractor (or its broker) confirming the Certificate of Insurance and required endorsements meet the hiring client's contractual insurance requirements, naming the exact endorsement forms.
templates.grounding_rule: Name the exact ISO/WC endorsement form numbers from the Insurance KB entries. Enforce the rule that the certificate alone is not proof — the endorsements must be attached. Never state Additional Insured applies to Workers' Compensation.

templates.purpose: Letter presenting three-year TRIR/DART performance to a hiring client, showing the calculation and benchmarking against the applicable BLS/NAICS average.
templates.grounding_rule: Use hours actually worked, not scheduled hours, and reconcile to the 300A. Pull the CURRENT BLS benchmark for the specific NAICS at generation time; do not hardcode a stale figure.

templates.purpose: Fill-in skeleton for ANY OSHA/DOT written program. The agent inserts the matching KB entry's required_elements as section headers, then drafts company-specific content under each.
templates.grounding_rule: REQUIRED_ELEMENTS, TRAINING_REQ, and RECORDKEEPING_REQ must be copied verbatim from the matching KB entry's required_elements, training, and recordkeeping fields. Every element in the KB entry must appear as a section; before returning, check the draft against the entry's failure_points.

templates.purpose: Fillable written OSHA Injury & Illness Recordkeeping Program (29 CFR 1904) — documents how the company keeps its 300/300A/301 accurately, the driver of TRIR/DART accuracy for prequal grading.
templates.grounding_rule: 29 CFR 1904 is public-domain; requirements stated in full. Recordability decisions govern the TRIR/DART prequal platforms grade — fill each [[...]] prompt with the company's own procedure and confirm no reviewer rejection reason applies.

templates.purpose: Energized Electrical Work Permit (EEWP) form (NFPA 70E 130.2 / 29 CFR 1910.333(a)) — authorizes and documents justified energized work with the shock/arc-flash assessment, PPE, and management approval.
templates.grounding_rule: Required for energized work inside the restricted approach or arc-flash boundary when equipment is NOT in an electrically safe work condition. Justification must be infeasibility or a greater hazard — never convenience. Management approval signed before work begins. Record assessment results; do not copy NFPA 70E tables.

templates.purpose: OSHA Forms 300 (Log), 300A (Annual Summary), and 301 (Incident Report) per 29 CFR 1904 — public-domain forms reproduced in full and ready to fill.
templates.grounding_rule: Enter each recordable case within 7 calendar days. Privacy-concern cases: no name on the 300 Log. The 300A must be certified by a company executive and posted Feb 1-Apr 30 even with zero cases. Retain all three forms 5 years.
